start_here: Say to your AI: "Make a send-only Resend key named Bakery newsletter and keep it as bakery-newsletter-key." It runs tool:make-a-sending-key with those two values.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it asks your email-sending account for a new send-only key and keeps that key in your vault under the name you give.
instructions: 1. Connect your Resend account once so your key is held under the name resend-api-key; the key is never typed into the request.

2. Choose a name Resend should show (1 to 50 characters) and a vault name keep_as (lower case letters, digits and dashes, for example bakery-newsletter-key). If that vault name is already held, nothing is asked and nothing is replaced.

3. Say to your AI: "Make a sending key named <name> and keep it as <keep_as>". It calls tools:run with tool tool:make-a-sending-key and {"name", "keep_as"}, plus domain_id to limit the key to one domain.
4. Read the answer: the new key's id and the held word in place of the key. The key itself is never shown; it sits in your vault under keep_as.
5. Later list keys with tool:list-sending-keys and turn one off with tool:remove-a-sending-key.

worked_examples.title: A send-only key kept as bakery-newsletter-key
worked_examples.ask: Make a send-only Resend key named Bakery newsletter and keep it as bakery-newsletter-key.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/email-sending-domains/tool-rows.json and test/list-email-sending-domains.test.mjs: the row POSTs https://api.resend.com/api-keys with {"name":"Bakery newsletter","permission":"sending_access"} and your key in the Authorization header; reply_holds_values moves the reply's token into your vault as bakery-newsletter-key.
